text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A policeman was killed and three others seriously injured when bandits suspected to be Ethiopians raided a village in the northeastern area of Lake Turkana.
- A Mombasa lawyer challenges President Moi to inform Kenyans under what rule or act he appointed High Court Judge Aaron Ringera, the Solicitor-General.
- Exiled Islamic preacher Sheikh Khalid Balala claims he will soon return to Kenya as the German government has processed his travel documents.
- Former minister Matthew Onyango Midika and Kisumu Rural member of parliament Professor Anyang' Nyongo undertake to woo former FORD-Kenya faction leader Raila Odinga to the Social Democratic Party.

- Air traffic controllers who have been on strike since Friday December 6 at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport are replaced with instructors from the school of Aviation and administrators from the Directorate of Civil Aviation.
- Democratic Party Chairman Mwai Kibaki says the current wave of thuggery gripping Kiambu district is an extended political plot involving ex-convicts, designed to cause chaos.
- Secret contacts to defuse the tension between Uganda and Zaire have taken place between Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni and special envoy Ngwanda of Zaire.
- Kenya is to be the site of a large-scale pilot programme to test the effectiveness of a new malaria drug found to be 98.5 percent effective in early field trials.
